---
# A page title, not decoration, and it does two jobs.
#
# 1. The metadata surfaces. Quarto composes `<title>`, `og:title` and
#    `twitter:title` from this plus the site title. With `title: ""` the two
#    social surfaces rendered as "– Robbins Analytics" — a dangling separator on
#    every shared card and every scrape of the landing page — while `<title>`
#    fell back to the bare site title. Every other page on the site carries a
#    title and rendered correctly; only the landing page did not.
#
# 2. The hero's own H1. With no title metadata, Quarto promotes the document's
#    first level-1 heading to be the title — so `# Aaron Robbins` was lifted OUT
#    of .hero-lede into the title block above the hero, and the hero rendered
#    starting at the subtitle with no name in it. Setting a title here leaves
#    the heading where it was written.
#
# `body-classes` is the third piece: with a title set, Quarto renders its own
# title block, which would restate the name twice. felix.scss hides it on
# felix-home (styles.scss did the same on hero-page). `title-block-style: none`
# is NOT the way to do that — it still emits the heading AND emits a second
# <header id="title-block-header">, which is a duplicate id and an axe failure.
title: "Aaron Robbins, AI Analytics Architect"
# The social titles are set explicitly because Quarto otherwise composes
# "<title> – <site title>" with an en dash; the spec (2026-10-14) wants a
# pipe on the cards. The <title> element itself keeps Quarto's composed form
# (`pagetitle:` does not remove the site title; tried 2026-10-14), which is
# what every other page carries. The description is the site-wide one in
# _quarto.yml, restated here so this page never falls back to anything else.
open-graph:
  title: "Aaron Robbins, AI Analytics Architect | Robbins Analytics"
  description: "AI analytics architecture portfolio, Aaron Robbins. Governed analytics, built with AI and proven by tests."
twitter-card:
  title: "Aaron Robbins, AI Analytics Architect | Robbins Analytics"
  description: "AI analytics architecture portfolio, Aaron Robbins. Governed analytics, built with AI and proven by tests."
# felix-home scopes the Felix page styling (paper, Inter, Inter Tight) to this
# page; see felix.scss. hero-page is kept so styles.scss's title-block rule
# still applies if felix.scss is ever removed.
body-classes: hero-page felix-home
image: https://www.robbinsanalytics.com/assets/thumb-portfolio.png
# custom, not full: the Felix sections carry their own 76rem container, and
# Quarto's page grid would add a second set of gutters around it.
page-layout: custom
toc: false
image-alt: "Cascadia module card — title, one-line summary, and the data source."
# Four listings over one inventory, one template. Quarto hands a custom
# template `items`, `template-params` and `utils`, never the listing itself,
# so each names its group here. The template always receives the whole
# inventory sorted by `order`, so a card's number is its position in the
# index whichever page it appears on. See _templates/fx-card.ejs.
listing:
  - id: fx-feature
    contents: data/portfolio.yml
    template: _templates/fx-card.ejs
    sort: "order"
    page-size: 100
    template-params:
      group: feature
      slug: build-by-build
      heading: h4
  - id: fx-leadership
    contents: data/portfolio.yml
    template: _templates/fx-card.ejs
    sort: "order"
    page-size: 100
    template-params:
      group: leadership
      slug: build-by-build
      heading: h4
  - id: fx-featured
    contents: data/portfolio.yml
    template: _templates/fx-card.ejs
    sort: "order"
    page-size: 100
    template-params:
      group: featured
      heading: h4
  - id: fx-beyond
    contents: data/portfolio.yml
    template: _templates/fx-card.ejs
    sort: "order"
    page-size: 100
    template-params:
      group: beyond
      heading: h4
---

::: {.hero-tagline}
12+ years turning messy data into decisions leaders trust: healthcare manufacturing and quality, ecommerce and retail, and time in supply chain, digital merchandising, and finance. The expertise is in the craft, not the tooling. I design the analytics, specify what correct looks like, and let AI do the build. Every build carries its own evidence: known answers set before the code, tests that run every time, and a record of what each test caught. That is proof stakeholders can check, not a claim they have to trust.
:::
